WEDDING SCAMMER: MARIO BOFFA

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A Wedding co-ordinator leaves a trail of tearful brides out of pocket with their big days potentially ruined.

Unique Selling Point:
CROOK EXPOSED
WE HAVE VIDEO CLIPS OF HIS VERSION

Summary:
Mario Boffa is a wedding coordinator and supplier who was one of the preferred vendors for a number of venues in Cape Town.

He ran into some financial difficulties in the midst of a drug addiction. He kept taking payments from brides, but stopped making the arrangements and booking the décor – leaving the brides broke and ruining a couple of wedding in the process.

His company’s gone in to voluntary liquidation, but Mario Boffa is making a comeback and we’re going to expose him before he ruins any more weddings.



Further information:
Mario Boffa was trading as Eventworx until mid-2019 and seems to have actually done a good job. According to case studies, he had great reviews and he even coordinated the wedding of Springbok rugby player Rudy Paige in May 2018 – the wedding was covered by Top Billing and I think Boffa was interviewed.

But mid-2019 something seems to have gone wrong. First Boffa re-marketed himself as Mozzafiato Weddings/Mozzafiato Flowers. He contacted all his current wedding clients and offered them a 15% discount on outstanding invoices, asking them to wrap up all outstanding payments as soon as possible. He continued to book new clients all the way up to November 2019. Then almost overnight, he disappeared. Apparently he sold all of his possessions (and emptied his warehouse), notified everyone that he was going into liquidation and vanished.

JANUARY 2020: Mario was in Thailand where he was trying to work as an English teacher. COVID-19 hit and Mario had to come home and face the music.

CASE STUDIES
• Riquel and Leigh Turner: this is the worst case. They had paid him R44 000 – almost the full bill – and he cancelled on them the night before the wedding. They then discovered that he hadn’t paid any of the suppliers he was supposed to book décor etc with. They had enlisted him to do their entire décor and coordination package, so most of the wedding seemed to be gone. They had to beg and plead with suppliers, use the previous night’s flowers, etc. He had met with them about a week before the wedding and gave no indication that anything was wrong, but they struggled to get hold of him in the days before the wedding. She’s going to send me the suppliers she knows of, as many of them are owed money as well. Apparently he used old invoices to suggest he had made new payments, and one supplier said he had become extremely unreliable in recent months. She reluctantly agreed to an interview.
• Chelton van Wyk and Zeta-Ann Olivier: they responded to a competition Boffa posted on Instagram in November and immediately paid a 50% deposit (R7100) at his insistence. On 1 December they got an email from him saying he was liquidating the business. They drove to various addresses he had listed and found that he had packed up and disappeared – one person told them he had done the same thing earlier when he changed from Eventworx to Mozzafiato.
• Kirsty Carras: she had paid Boffa a total of R29 000, of which some came from her father’s pension. Their total quote was R40 000. She discussed payments with him the day before he announced his liquidation to them and he gave no indication of anything being wrong. She got confirmation that his liquidation had not been finalised – in fact, the company he claimed was liquidating him had never heard of him when Kirsty phoned. She tried to get the sheriff to attach his possessions but the warehouse was already empty.
• Kim Kelly Dalais: he went into liquidation only two weeks before her wedding. She seems to have got married anyway as well. Found Hellopeter review.


RIPPED OFF SUPPLIERS
We have a list of at least 7 suppliers that didn’t receive payment for services delivered to Mario’s company – they are all based in CPT

LIQUIDATION
The liquidation application was made and it had been to court – but it is not yet finalised.

MARIO’S TEARFUL EXPLANATION
Dear Mario likes to share his version – we have video clips of him telling his side of the story… he breaks down and speaks in a teary voice…shame. He claims in an epic Facebook post that 2019 was his most challenging year – stopped taking a salary and was putting money in to the business to survive and eventually had to retrench staff – but eventually he found comfort in Crystal Meth and became addicted.

WHAT NOW?
Mario is back in action – well he’s trying to get up and running again – he registered a new wedding co-ordination business – EVENTEUR – using the same contact number he had before.

He is still in JHB, he contacted the travel co-ordinator that’s our snitch on Saturday asking when the next bus was going down to Cape Town – our snitch will confirm with me later today.

WHAT WE HAVE
The video clips are great. That’s enough to cover us in terms of a right of reply – should he decline and an interview.

HOW WE DO IT
1. Set up to do the interviews with presenter via Skype, call him in the morning requesting interview while we know he is still in JHB – he is arrogant enough to do it, he believes he is the victim here, his track record shows he is desperate to clear his name whenever there are allegations. If he agrees, we set up to shoot it that afternoon. If not, we go at him on the phone until he drops the call. WE HAVE THE VIDEO CLIPS OF HIM EXPLAINING HIS SIDE OF THE STORY – NOT A TRAIN SMASH IF HE SAYS NO.
2. We wait to find out if he is going to book a bus trip and we try to doorstop him there. Challenges – it could take a while before he commits to going back down to CPT if he decided to do it. Also, he seems to be indecisive about it – first he was going to CPT, then last week he was staying in JHB to try to get work, a few days later he wanted to go to CPT again. This has the potential to be messy because there will be lots of other people, the bus leaves from either Emporer’s or Monte – which means we’ll have issues with cameras and filming.
3. We can try to contact him via his new business and see if we can do a sting if he agrees – usually I would vote for this – but these aren’t normal circumstances – weddings aren’t happening like they used to, so the story won’t be that believable.

** HE HAS LAWYERED UP IN THE PAST, AND WILL POSSIBLY TRY WITH US AS WELL.

MY SUGGESTION
Once it’s commissioned, we call to set up meeting for wedding planner, hopefully do the undercover. If we are successful, we set up to meet him with the groom and then we bust him. If it’s not successful, we call him and ask for interview. I’m not a fan of the bus trip option – too much that can go wrong - this could be messy.

Script:


WEDDING PLANNER SCRIPT

VO: Tying the knot is something most couples aspire to, and for many brides-to-be it’s one of the biggest events in their lives.

LINK: It’s all about the décor and the detail – bridal couples plot, plan and save hard earned cash, investing in making their dream day a reality, but it can quickly be derailed if the wedding planner is not above board.

VO: A lesson Zeta-Ann Olivier and her fiance Chelton van Wyk, learnt the hard way, when they bought a Black Friday Flash Sale in November last year .

ZETA: What this offered was twelve guess tables, a main table, two large flower arrangements and the main tables flowers was everything that we were looking at in one package.

VO: The deal was being offered by one of the Western Cape’s established wedding co-ordinators – Mario Boffa of Mozzafiato. By the age of 29, he’s done celebrity weddings, been featured on lifestyle shows and was a preferred service provider for some top wedding venues.

Keen to secure the deal, the couple quickly paid a 50% deposit of just over R 7000 [R7186.50 ] on the 25th of November and booked a consultation with Mario for four days later.

ZETA: When he received payment he postponed that initial appointment. So he said he is not available on the twenty ninth anymore. He has an event on the 30th.

VO: That event, was the wedding of Riquel and Leigh Turner. The couple had paid Mario over R44000 [R44459,20] for his co-ordination and décor services.

RIQUEL: We really just want a one stop shop. // And Mario really stood out in that way because he did not coordination. He did take all literally everything that makes up your wedding. And we found that he was quite trusted in that industry.

VO: But Riquel & Leigh would realise their trust was be misplaced at the 11th hour. They received an email from Mario on the 29th of November .

RIQUEL: Literally I think two o'clock the Friday, the wedding was the next day //There was a notice of you know liquidation unable to assist you for your wedding day //And I was literally shattered

VO: The letter read: “Due to financial difficulty and the company being over indebted. We have exhausted all financial resources and we will be liquidating.”

Zeta & Chelton received a similar letter, dated just 3 days after they had paid the deposit.

ZETA: I felt like I was having a panic attack at that stage.

VO: They called, emailed and messaged – but could not get hold of Mario. In desperation they went to the business address.

ZETA: Everything was removed all the phony charges the logo was the No Mario

VO: Mario Boffa had packed up and was heading for Thailand, to take up a teaching position.

But his new career would be shortlived. COVID-19 hit Thailand in January and soon Mario found himself unemployed, stranded and in the spotlight - when he tried to raise funds for a repatriation flight for South Africans stuck in Thailand.

UPSOUND MARIO IN THAILAND
MARIO: I assure you I will do everything in my power to make sure that we take home two hundred and sixty three citizens that are stranded in Thailand.

VO: But Mario’s past caught up with him. When he started getting backlash from disgruntled brides, he posted this clip explaining his situation.

UPSOUND MARIO IN THAILAND
MARIO: my company was liquidated so it was bankrupt and I had to go through a
voluntary liquidation // I lost the company and I'm still being crucified for it. Months later.

VO: No Mario, the liquidation is not final yet. Attorney, Colin Strime, explains, getting into liquidation is easy, finalising it, is a different ball game.

COLIN: The process of the winding up from the liquidator takes control to the time that he finishes in deed registers the company at the end of the day. That takes time.

MARIO: //I wish I had the funds to refund all of the brides who did lose their money. But unfortunately I don't. I would never be able to return back to the wedding and events industry because of my reputation that got trashed.

 
VO: The brides aren’t buying Mario’s tearful message.

Attorney Kirsty Carras and her fiancé Chris Williams, paid Mario over R28000 [28087.03] during the course of 2019 and were set to pay another R10 000 shortly before Mario dropped the liquidation bomb.

KIRSTY: I struggled to sympathize with him// he happily took our money and never once expressed to us you know that there was an issue even a few days before the liquidation notices came he was more than happy to take our money

VO: She tried to issue a legal summons, but all the company assets had already been removed.. Kirsty also contacted the appointed liquidators.

KIRSTY: // They actually confirmed to me that it is still in process. They are still busy with the creditors meetings.

VO: Mario had returned to South Africa and spoke to us from his empty Cape Town house.

MARIO: You know I cannot comment on every single client. What exactly happened. I don't have those files in front of me. I dealt with about 45 brides // per month. And I can't remember what all of them looked like what their second names are.

VO: Mario says his troubles started in early 2019 when SARS hit the company with a bill for import duties, his business partner resigned and he claims the company went into business rescue amidst declining bookings in the winter season.

MASA: So does this mean you dipping into the clients deposits To try and rescue business?
MARIO: Yes. Yeah. That's exactly what happened. //because of monthly overheads and things that the business required

VO: Besides retrenching staff, Mario claims he also used just over a million rand of his personal finances to keep the business afloat.

ZETA: He's claiming to play the part of a victim we knowingly took money from us and he knew he was not going to provide a service. And it's money that we worked hard for.

VO: According to Mario, the ad Zeta-Anne responded to was prepaid and scheduled to run.

MARIO: I don't I don't remember the client sorry no comment on the client

MASA: don’t recall taking deposits the week beofre liquidation?
MARIO You know I don't recall because the business was split up into teams. // So I did not work with the accounts of the business as such

VO: But so-called ignorance is not going to fly here – Mario could be held liable in his personal capacity explains Strime.

COLIN: If the person under those circumstances took the money knowing that they were not going to deliver they started the ballgame and that they had no intention of repaying the money then that amounts to reckless trading // that person could be rendered personally liable To that bride for all the debts of the company. It's a penalty in fact not just what she's lost but all the debts of the company in terms of the section

VO: It appears that while Mario kept taking payments from brides, he stopped making the arrangements and booking the décor.

With Riquel and Leigh’s– Mario claimed some suppliers were booked and paid for – but that was not the case .

RIQUEL: When we had cold baby what told actually those invoices are old or no that's not the case it did not secure it. It wasn't paid for again. So it was you know we were just left with a whole lot of nothing again

MARIO: Once we went into the liquidation the bank froze all the bank accounts. So I don't know if it was because it is a transfer between different banks that it was part of the seizing and freezing process and they refused to allow the funds to go out. I really don't know what happened with that.

VO: Riquel & Leigh’s big day was saved by family jumping in to help, the venue’s management and the kindness of other wedding planners who donated décor and flowers from weddings done on the previous day. Despite the agony and stress caused Mario – their day was still magical.

MASA: Admit you did not pay fr it.
MARIO: I don't have records to check it and I'm not going to comment on it /… which I don’t have facts on

LINK: But it’s not just clients that were dropped, suppliers that provided décor and flowers for weddings planned by Mario were also left out of pocket with unpaid bills worth thousands of rands.

VO: Brad Stephenson from Three Buds supplied Mario with imported flowers. The total outstanding bill is still at R24,676

BRAD: He would pay a small amount just to be able to get the next order//. You need the roses to carry on and it's going to settle in for the end of this next week. It was just kind of excuse optics excuse just delaying payment

VO: Payment Promises Mario now has no memory of.

MARIO: that I don't recall.

VO: We’ll jog your memory – in addition to emails promising payments, Mario also sent this voice note.

UPSOUND MARIO VOICE NOTE: I’m trying to get that sorted… I hate owing people money.

VO: But Mario never made good on that… Bradley says the non-payment has had a crippling effect on his business.

BRAD: He'd put us in a really terrible position. I'm quite angry that he’s done it to so many people /the long and short of it is I'm sure they're going to be other companies that are bankrupt to liquidate just just because of this

VO: By Mario’s estimation, a list of clients, suppliers and banks are owed just over R1,2 million. He claims he’s been subjected to threats from clients . An allegation Kirsty denies.

KIRSTY: I posted my story on Facebook to get the word out there and he responded and said to me watch out what you're doing. I'm going to sue you for defamation. And then subsequently blocked me.

VO: Essentially Kirsty and Chris will be paying double for their wedding planning and décor with nothing to show for the R28 000 they paid Mario.

MASA: So she gifted you R28k
MARIO: No she doesn't see it. She didn't give me anything. She prepaid for services. And the business was liquidated.
** MASA DOESN’T RESPOND SAYING ANYTHING SNAPPY ABOUT THE LIQUIDATION NOT BEING FINALISED

KIRSTY: We will never get our money back. But. I think he just needs to look at himself and really acknowledge what he's done to a lot of the couples that were affected.

VO: In May, Mario attempted a comeback to the wedding industry when he set up a new business venture .

MASA: Can you start the same company as what he had been liquidator for a week still owes people money is that allowed?
COLIN: Yes it's a brand new company and He's in South Africa. You can form a company with little or no capital and start the business again.

VO: Strime explains, while it could be costly to pursue the director of the company and the payouts from the liquidation are not guaranteed, it is still an option for people who are owed money.

COLIN: I think it's important that creditors. Are not apathetic and those who have lost money. Take steps which are available to them legally// and try and render the management the directors those who are responsible for their loss personally liable with the company for the debt

KIRSTY: if he's up and running with a new company. I see no reason why he should not be in a position to pay back the couples that lost a lot of money to him.

VO: But Mario says that business is now on hold.

MARIO: That should would have been based in Johannesburg because of the liquidation of event. I would never be able to rebuild relationships and gain faith in the wedding and events industry in the Western Cape.

ZETA: What he did was wasn't can I say to a certain extent an injustice to us because this was a day we'd dreamed of and to an extent stole some of our joys of planning our wedding.
MASA: Would you recommend him?
RIQUEL: No , not at all – unfortunately not.


 
PROMOS
PROMO 1
VO: After selling dream weddings, a well-known wedding co-ordinator raked in deposits, promised big and delivered very little – leaving a trail of angry brides out of pocket and their big day in ruins.

NEW PROMO 2
VO: A trusted wedding co-ordinator rakes in deposits but fails to deliver the dream weddings he promised, leaving behind a trail of angry brides – out of pocket and their perfect wedding plans derailed.

PROMO 3
VO: Imagine your dream wedding – the décor, the detail – and then the day before walking down the aisle your wedding planner – dumps you with nothing organised – leaving you broke and your big day in ruins.








EXTRA MARIO POINTS
- claimed he sold a portion of the business, they took the décor stock but didn’t pay in full – I asked for the company details and he sent a voice note saying he can’t tell me the name – so it can’t be verified.

mihle@combinedartists.co.za 23 June 2020 Script: WEDDING PLANNER SCRIPT VO: Tying the knot is something most couples aspire to, and for many brides-to-be it’s one of the biggest events in their lives. LINK: It’s all about the décor and the detail – bridal couples plot, plan and save hard earned cash, investing in making their dream day a reality, but it can quickly be derailed if the wedding planner is not above board. VO: A lesson Zeta-Ann Olivier and her fiance Chelton van Wyk, learnt the hard way, when they bought a Black Friday Flash Sale in November last year . ZETA: What this offered was twelve guess tables, a main table, two large flower arrangements and the main tables flowers was everything that we were looking at in one package. VO: The deal was being offered by one of the Western Cape’s established wedding co-ordinators – Mario Boffa of Mozzafiato. By the age of 29, he’s done celebrity weddings, been featured on lifestyle shows and was a preferred service provider for some top wedding venues. Keen to secure the deal, the couple quickly paid a 50% deposit of just over R 7000 [R7186.50 ] on the 25th of November and booked a consultation with Mario for four days later. ZETA: When he received payment he postponed that initial appointment. So he said he is not available on the twenty ninth anymore. He has an event on the 30th. VO: That event, was the wedding of Riquel and Leigh Turner. The couple had paid Mario over R44000 [R44459,20] for his co-ordination and décor services. RIQUEL: We really just want a one stop shop. // And Mario really stood out in that way because he did not coordination. He did take all literally everything that makes up your wedding. And we found that he was quite trusted in that industry. VO: But Riquel & Leigh would realise their trust was be misplaced at the 11th hour. They received an email from Mario on the 29th of November . RIQUEL: Literally I think two o'clock the Friday, the wedding was the next day //There was a notice of you know liquidation unable to assist you for your wedding day //And I was literally shattered VO: The letter read: “Due to financial difficulty and the company being over indebted. We have exhausted all financial resources and we will be liquidating.” Zeta & Chelton received a similar letter, dated just 3 days after they had paid the deposit. ZETA: I felt like I was having a panic attack at that stage. VO: They called, emailed and messaged – but could not get hold of Mario. In desperation they went to the business address. ZETA: Everything was removed all the phony charges the logo was the No Mario VO: Mario Boffa had packed up and was heading for Thailand, to take up a teaching position. But his new career would be shortlived. COVID-19 hit Thailand in January and soon Mario found himself unemployed, stranded and in the spotlight - when he tried to raise funds for a repatriation flight for South Africans stuck in Thailand. UPSOUND MARIO IN THAILAND MARIO: I assure you I will do everything in my power to make sure that we take home two hundred and sixty three citizens that are stranded in Thailand. VO: But Mario’s past caught up with him. When he started getting backlash from disgruntled brides, he posted this clip explaining his situation. UPSOUND MARIO IN THAILAND MARIO: my company was liquidated so it was bankrupt and I had to go through a voluntary liquidation // I lost the company and I'm still being crucified for it. Months later. VO: No Mario, the liquidation is not final yet. Attorney, Colin Strime, explains, getting into liquidation is easy, finalising it, is a different ball game. COLIN: The process of the winding up from the liquidator takes control to the time that he finishes in deed registers the company at the end of the day. That takes time. MARIO: //I wish I had the funds to refund all of the brides who did lose their money. But unfortunately I don't. I would never be able to return back to the wedding and events industry because of my reputation that got trashed. VO: The brides aren’t buying Mario’s tearful message. Attorney Kirsty Carras and her fiancé Chris Williams, paid Mario over R28000 [28087.03] during the course of 2019 and were set to pay another R10 000 shortly before Mario dropped the liquidation bomb. KIRSTY: I struggled to sympathize with him// he happily took our money and never once expressed to us you know that there was an issue even a few days before the liquidation notices came he was more than happy to take our money VO: She tried to issue a legal summons, but all the company assets had already been removed.. Kirsty also contacted the appointed liquidators. KIRSTY: // They actually confirmed to me that it is still in process. They are still busy with the creditors meetings. VO: Mario had returned to South Africa and spoke to us from his empty Cape Town house. MARIO: You know I cannot comment on every single client. What exactly happened. I don't have those files in front of me. I dealt with about 45 brides // per month. And I can't remember what all of them looked like what their second names are. VO: Mario says his troubles started in early 2019 when SARS hit the company with a bill for import duties, his business partner resigned and he claims the company went into business rescue amidst declining bookings in the winter season. MASA: So does this mean you dipping into the clients deposits To try and rescue business? MARIO: Yes. Yeah. That's exactly what happened. //because of monthly overheads and things that the business required VO: Besides retrenching staff, Mario claims he also used just over a million rand of his personal finances to keep the business afloat. ZETA: He's claiming to play the part of a victim we knowingly took money from us and he knew he was not going to provide a service. And it's money that we worked hard for. VO: According to Mario, the ad Zeta-Anne responded to was prepaid and scheduled to run. MARIO: I don't I don't remember the client sorry no comment on the client MASA: don’t recall taking deposits the week beofre liquidation? MARIO You know I don't recall because the business was split up into teams. // So I did not work with the accounts of the business as such VO: But so-called ignorance is not going to fly here – Mario could be held liable in his personal capacity explains Strime. COLIN: If the person under those circumstances took the money knowing that they were not going to deliver they started the ballgame and that they had no intention of repaying the money then that amounts to reckless trading // that person could be rendered personally liable To that bride for all the debts of the company. It's a penalty in fact not just what she's lost but all the debts of the company in terms of the section VO: It appears that while Mario kept taking payments from brides, he stopped making the arrangements and booking the décor. With Riquel and Leigh’s– Mario claimed some suppliers were booked and paid for – but that was not the case . RIQUEL: When we had cold baby what told actually those invoices are old or no that's not the case it did not secure it. It wasn't paid for again. So it was you know we were just left with a whole lot of nothing again MARIO: Once we went into the liquidation the bank froze all the bank accounts. So I don't know if it was because it is a transfer between different banks that it was part of the seizing and freezing process and they refused to allow the funds to go out. I really don't know what happened with that. VO: Riquel & Leigh’s big day was saved by family jumping in to help, the venue’s management and the kindness of other wedding planners who donated décor and flowers from weddings done on the previous day. Despite the agony and stress caused Mario – their day was still magical. MASA: Admit you did not pay fr it. MARIO: I don't have records to check it and I'm not going to comment on it /… which I don’t have facts on LINK: But it’s not just clients that were dropped, suppliers that provided décor and flowers for weddings planned by Mario were also left out of pocket with unpaid bills worth thousands of rands. VO: Brad Stephenson from Three Buds supplied Mario with imported flowers. The total outstanding bill is still at R24,676 BRAD: He would pay a small amount just to be able to get the next order//. You need the roses to carry on and it's going to settle in for the end of this next week. It was just kind of excuse optics excuse just delaying payment VO: Payment Promises Mario now has no memory of. MARIO: that I don't recall. VO: We’ll jog your memory – in addition to emails promising payments, Mario also sent this voice note. UPSOUND MARIO VOICE NOTE: I’m trying to get that sorted… I hate owing people money. VO: But Mario never made good on that… Bradley says the non-payment has had a crippling effect on his business. BRAD: He'd put us in a really terrible position. I'm quite angry that he’s done it to so many people /the long and short of it is I'm sure they're going to be other companies that are bankrupt to liquidate just just because of this VO: By Mario’s estimation, a list of clients, suppliers and banks are owed just over R1,2 million. He claims he’s been subjected to threats from clients . An allegation Kirsty denies. KIRSTY: I posted my story on Facebook to get the word out there and he responded and said to me watch out what you're doing. I'm going to sue you for defamation. And then subsequently blocked me. VO: Essentially Kirsty and Chris will be paying double for their wedding planning and décor with nothing to show for the R28 000 they paid Mario. MASA: So she gifted you R28k MARIO: No she doesn't see it. She didn't give me anything. She prepaid for services. And the business was liquidated. ** MASA DOESN’T RESPOND SAYING ANYTHING SNAPPY ABOUT THE LIQUIDATION NOT BEING FINALISED KIRSTY: We will never get our money back. But. I think he just needs to look at himself and really acknowledge what he's done to a lot of the couples that were affected. VO: In May, Mario attempted a comeback to the wedding industry when he set up a new business venture . MASA: Can you start the same company as what he had been liquidator for a week still owes people money is that allowed? COLIN: Yes it's a brand new company and He's in South Africa. You can form a company with little or no capital and start the business again. VO: Strime explains, while it could be costly to pursue the director of the company and the payouts from the liquidation are not guaranteed, it is still an option for people who are owed money. COLIN: I think it's important that creditors. Are not apathetic and those who have lost money. Take steps which are available to them legally// and try and render the management the directors those who are responsible for their loss personally liable with the company for the debt KIRSTY: if he's up and running with a new company. I see no reason why he should not be in a position to pay back the couples that lost a lot of money to him. VO: But Mario says that business is now on hold. MARIO: That should would have been based in Johannesburg because of the liquidation of event. I would never be able to rebuild relationships and gain faith in the wedding and events industry in the Western Cape. ZETA: What he did was wasn't can I say to a certain extent an injustice to us because this was a day we'd dreamed of and to an extent stole some of our joys of planning our wedding. MASA: Would you recommend him? RIQUEL: No , not at all – unfortunately not. PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: After selling dream weddings, a well-known wedding co-ordinator raked in deposits, promised big and delivered very little – leaving a trail of angry brides out of pocket and their big day in ruins. NEW PROMO 2 VO: A trusted wedding co-ordinator rakes in deposits but fails to deliver the dream weddings he promised, leaving behind a trail of angry brides – out of pocket and their perfect wedding plans derailed. PROMO 3 VO: Imagine your dream wedding – the décor, the detail – and then the day before walking down the aisle your wedding planner – dumps you with nothing organised – leaving you broke and your big day in ruins. EXTRA MARIO POINTS - claimed he sold a portion of the business, they took the décor stock but didn’t pay in full – I asked for the company details and he sent a voice note saying he can’t tell me the name – so it can’t be verified. -

metadata.Summary: Mario Boffa is a wedding coordinator and supplier who was one of the preferred vendors for a number of venues in Cape Town. He ran into some financial difficulties in the midst of a drug addiction. He kept taking payments from brides, but stopped making the arrangements and booking the décor – leaving the brides broke and ruining a couple of wedding in the process. His company’s gone in to voluntary liquidation, but Mario Boffa is making a comeback and we’re going to expose him before he ruins any more weddings.
metadata.Further information: Mario Boffa was trading as Eventworx until mid-2019 and seems to have actually done a good job. According to case studies, he had great reviews and he even coordinated the wedding of Springbok rugby player Rudy Paige in May 2018 – the wedding was covered by Top Billing and I think Boffa was interviewed. But mid-2019 something seems to have gone wrong. First Boffa re-marketed himself as Mozzafiato Weddings/Mozzafiato Flowers. He contacted all his current wedding clients and offered them a 15% discount on outstanding invoices, asking them to wrap up all outstanding payments as soon as possible. He continued to book new clients all the way up to November 2019. Then almost overnight, he disappeared. Apparently he sold all of his possessions (and emptied his warehouse), notified everyone that he was going into liquidation and vanished. JANUARY 2020: Mario was in Thailand where he was trying to work as an English teacher. COVID-19 hit and Mario had to come home and face the music. CASE STUDIES • Riquel and Leigh Turner: this is the worst case. They had paid him R44 000 – almost the full bill – and he cancelled on them the night before the wedding. They then discovered that he hadn’t paid any of the suppliers he was supposed to book décor etc with. They had enlisted him to do their entire décor and coordination package, so most of the wedding seemed to be gone. They had to beg and plead with suppliers, use the previous night’s flowers, etc. He had met with them about a week before the wedding and gave no indication that anything was wrong, but they struggled to get hold of him in the days before the wedding. She’s going to send me the suppliers she knows of, as many of them are owed money as well. Apparently he used old invoices to suggest he had made new payments, and one supplier said he had become extremely unreliable in recent months. She reluctantly agreed to an interview. • Chelton van Wyk and Zeta-Ann Olivier: they responded to a competition Boffa posted on Instagram in November and immediately paid a 50% deposit (R7100) at his insistence. On 1 December they got an email from him saying he was liquidating the business. They drove to various addresses he had listed and found that he had packed up and disappeared – one person told them he had done the same thing earlier when he changed from Eventworx to Mozzafiato. • Kirsty Carras: she had paid Boffa a total of R29 000, of which some came from her father’s pension. Their total quote was R40 000. She discussed payments with him the day before he announced his liquidation to them and he gave no indication of anything being wrong. She got confirmation that his liquidation had not been finalised – in fact, the company he claimed was liquidating him had never heard of him when Kirsty phoned. She tried to get the sheriff to attach his possessions but the warehouse was already empty. • Kim Kelly Dalais: he went into liquidation only two weeks before her wedding. She seems to have got married anyway as well. Found Hellopeter review. RIPPED OFF SUPPLIERS We have a list of at least 7 suppliers that didn’t receive payment for services delivered to Mario’s company – they are all based in CPT LIQUIDATION The liquidation application was made and it had been to court – but it is not yet finalised. MARIO’S TEARFUL EXPLANATION Dear Mario likes to share his version – we have video clips of him telling his side of the story… he breaks down and speaks in a teary voice…shame. He claims in an epic Facebook post that 2019 was his most challenging year – stopped taking a salary and was putting money in to the business to survive and eventually had to retrench staff – but eventually he found comfort in Crystal Meth and became addicted. WHAT NOW? Mario is back in action – well he’s trying to get up and running again – he registered a new wedding co-ordination business – EVENTEUR – using the same contact number he had before. He is still in JHB, he contacted the travel co-ordinator that’s our snitch on Saturday asking when the next bus was going down to Cape Town – our snitch will confirm with me later today. WHAT WE HAVE The video clips are great. That’s enough to cover us in terms of a right of reply – should he decline and an interview. HOW WE DO IT 1. Set up to do the interviews with presenter via Skype, call him in the morning requesting interview while we know he is still in JHB – he is arrogant enough to do it, he believes he is the victim here, his track record shows he is desperate to clear his name whenever there are allegations. If he agrees, we set up to shoot it that afternoon. If not, we go at him on the phone until he drops the call. WE HAVE THE VIDEO CLIPS OF HIM EXPLAINING HIS SIDE OF THE STORY – NOT A TRAIN SMASH IF HE SAYS NO. 2. We wait to find out if he is going to book a bus trip and we try to doorstop him there. Challenges – it could take a while before he commits to going back down to CPT if he decided to do it. Also, he seems to be indecisive about it – first he was going to CPT, then last week he was staying in JHB to try to get work, a few days later he wanted to go to CPT again. This has the potential to be messy because there will be lots of other people, the bus leaves from either Emporer’s or Monte – which means we’ll have issues with cameras and filming. 3. We can try to contact him via his new business and see if we can do a sting if he agrees – usually I would vote for this – but these aren’t normal circumstances – weddings aren’t happening like they used to, so the story won’t be that believable. ** HE HAS LAWYERED UP IN THE PAST, AND WILL POSSIBLY TRY WITH US AS WELL. MY SUGGESTION Once it’s commissioned, we call to set up meeting for wedding planner, hopefully do the undercover. If we are successful, we set up to meet him with the groom and then we bust him. If it’s not successful, we call him and ask for interview. I’m not a fan of the bus trip option – too much that can go wrong - this could be messy.
